newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower as earlier weakness on the December contract continued in late trading after a wave of commission-house selling. The benchmark contract extended earlier losses to end down US$6.60 at US$331.90 per tonne, having turned over 1,357 lots and the March contract was US$4.80 lower at US$332.00 on a volume of 1,110 lots. Raw sugar futures in New York settled near the day's lows on residual speculative liquidation and selling of the October/March spread, market sources said. The October/March spread narrowed to 0.16 compared to 0.19 cents/lb at Friday's close while the October contract, down for the fourth consecutive day, managed to hold above key support seen at 11.50 cents/lb. October closed at 11.57 cents/lb, while March ended four points lower at 11.41 cents/lb. All other positions ended unchanged to 11 points higher.

CHINA - Chinese sugar production in August 1996 amounted to a mere 9,692 tonnes, raw value, against 4,234 tonnes in August 1995. This brought total production in 1995/96 (September/August) up to 6.55 million tonnes against 5.90 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 6.54 million tonnes in 1993/94.

GERMANY - The latest German beet test results of September 13, 1996 showed satisfactory increases in both sugar content and beet weight. Beet weight per ha rose by 6.76 tonnes to 57.87 tonnes compared to 55.68 tonnes in 1995 and the five-year average (1991/95) of 55.66 tonnes. Sugar content rose by 1.5 percentage points to 16.8 per cent against 15.8 per cent in 1995 and the average of 16.2 per cent. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 9.71 tonnes per ha, more than 10 per cent above last year's result of 8.79 tonnes and also above the five-year average of 9.03 tonnes. The good weight of foliage and the rather high number of plants per ha suggest that the crop is in good shape and that a rather satisfactory output level is on the cards.

FINLAND - Sugar exports in April 1996 amounted to 2,297 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 312 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first seven months of 1995/96 (October/April) up to 34,078 tonnes againt 4,551 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 reached 6,763 tonnes against 15,127 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/April 1995/96 were Uzbekisten with 9,937 tonnes whites against nil, Russia with 8,415 tonnes compared to 430 tonnes and Estonia with 8,076 tonnes, up from 713 tonnes. Sugar imports in October/April 1995/96 were negligible (1,257 tonnes).

AUSTRALIA - The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has increased its forecast of Australian sugar production to 5.49 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July/June), up from its previous forecast of 5.13 million tonnes. According to ABARE, the significant increase can be attributed mainly to improved rainfall and an increase in area planted, including the establishment of sugar production in the Ord River Region of western Australia. Australian sugar exports are forecast to rise by 7.9 per cent to 4.30 million tonnes in 1996/97, ABARE said in its latest forecast. However, a stronger Australian dollar and low world sugar prices mean that average returns to Australian producers are forecast to fall by 7.5 per cent in 1996/97 to A$335 per tonne, ABARE added.

The Egyptian state's Sugar and Integrated Industries Company cancelled a tender for 25,000 tonnes of raw or white sugar on Monday, saying it received only one bid at US$326.00 a tonne for raw sugar. A company official said the company might invite new bids at a later stage. Monday's tender was for October delivery. A trader said the sole bid was from Louis Dreyfus. Other sugar dealers were not interested because the Egyptian company is imposing terms that are too onerous, especially on certification of the sugar by health authorities, it was added.
